selections.description: Shared webhook authentication/deserialization, stream/cancellation utilities and cloud lifetime semantics with original tests and explicit Worker adaptations.
acceptance: Authenticate untouched request bytes before parsing/hydration; preserve legacy v0 prefix requirements and Standard Webhooks as a local extension, explicit schemes, replay bounds, key rotation and typed failures. Invalid signatures never invoke handlers.

Web Request delivery awaits async callbacks and propagates their failures; unknown normalized envelopes are rejected, not silently acknowledged. Preserve canonical space/phone and multipart targets through deserialization and actionable hydration.

Adapt supported original deserialize, webhook and stream utility scenarios into executable public API tests. Evaluate advanced content/event mappings against the native and normalized wire contracts; report precise missing fields/contracts rather than fabricating parity.

Bounded lazy iteration preserves backpressure, abort/return cleanup, pending-consumer settlement and error propagation across multiple consumers and line refresh. Reuse existing app lifetime and credential inventory, not a second stream owner.

Fusor/resumable source and original tests are watched semantic evidence: adopt isolated Web-safe improvements when justified, but unsupported full services/replay/reconnect need an explicit contract/architecture blocker and must not be labeled passed.

api, webhooks and imessage remain independently usable; real packed workerd consumers pass without Node/Bun globals or nodejs_compat. Preserve original manifest pins and meaningful existing tests; new ports include executable assertions and docs/ports immutable source/test URLs, original SHA-256 hashes and adaptation/blocker receipts.

instructions.goal: Track and implement supported shared delivery/security/cancellation behavior with original upstream tests, preserving deliberate Worker webhook and lifecycle differences.
adaptation: Read docs/UPSTREAM-COMPATIBILITY.md and docs/COMPATIBILITY-PLAN.md. Baseline is acknowledged partial adoption, not parity. Do not turn upstream fire-and-forget acknowledgements, bare-hex signatures or cache-first metadata into regressions in the Web facade.

Shared platform/Fusor/utility/test-support sources are semantic dependencies. Reuse one SpectrumLines inventory, one app lifetime, authoritative native lookup and bounded native broadcast rather than transplanting a registry/framework or private Node mocks.

All four independent packages must retain public identity and supported signatures. New dependency/package/export-map needs must be documented as architecture decisions in docs/ports and separately approved; manifests, scripts and verification remain protected.

Supported improvements require actual runtime and regression-test artifacts; record precise wire-contract, provider or host-lifetime blockers instead of blanket documentation-only success or invented behavior.
nonGoals: Other providers, local Apple DB/macOS integrations, environment discovery, automatic telemetry and wholesale upstream framework transplantation.
Node/Bun polyfills, Buffer, nodejs_compat, full unreviewed Fusor services, automatic reconnection/catch-up replay and upstream framework adapters instead of the Web Request API.

preserve: Update current usage and compatibility documentation when behavior changes, while retaining original test attribution, license notices and historical baseline coverage. New support is not evidence that old tests were rebased.
Preserve existing SDK work, supported public names/signatures, raw Uint8Array and standalone package ownership. Only standard Web APIs and existing management/binary gRPC-Web contracts are allowed.

One SpectrumLines inventory/app lifetime; authoritative uncached getMessage; canonical phone/space guards; multipart identities; authenticated byte-exact awaited webhook handlers; bounded lazy iterators with error/cancel propagation.

Never delete, skip, weaken or replace meaningful tests, bypass protected boundary/provenance/audit checks via fixtures or test-specific runtime branches, or rewrite original tests/upstream-manifest.json pins. Record new partial-port links/hashes and executable target tests under docs/ports; test counts and reports alone establish no parity.
Do not modify manifests, lockfiles, scripts, CI, policy/check runners or source-audit logic. New dependencies/packages/export-map changes need human approval outside this policy.
